questions.markingGuide: Evaluate the expression inside the square root first: 2.5 × 0.9659 = 2.41475. Then 2.41475 / 9.81 = 0.24615. Square root: √0.24615 = 0.49614. Multiply by π: T = π × 0.49614 = 1.5587. Accept rounding to 1.559 or 1.56. Award Achieved for correct answer with or without working shown. Accept ± minor rounding differences.

questions.text:
[Diagram: A cylinder with radius 4.5 cm and height 15 cm. A label wraps around the curved surface only (not covering the circular top or bottom).]

12 identical cylindrical tins each have radius 4.5 cm and height 15 cm. Each tin has a label that wraps around its curved surface (not covering the top or bottom). Find the total area of all 12 labels.
questions.markingGuide: The label wraps around the curved surface of the cylinder (not the top or bottom). Area of one label = circumference × height = 2πr × h = 2π × 4.5 × 15 = 135π = 424.115 cm². Total area of 12 labels = 12 × 424.115 = 5089.38 cm². Accept exact answer 1620π cm². Achieved = correct area of one label, OR total area with a minor error in working. Merit = correct total area of all 12 labels with clear working.

questions.text:
[Diagram: A rectangular box containing 12 cylinders arranged in rows. Each cylinder has radius p and height 15. The box fits tightly around all 12 tins.]

The 12 tins are packed into a rectangular box. Each tin has radius p cm. The volume of one tin is 15πp². The volume of the box is 720p². Find the proportion of space inside the box that is empty, and show that it is independent of the radius p.
questions.markingGuide: Volume of 12 tins = 12 × 15πp² = 180πp². Volume of empty space = Volume of box – Volume of 12 tins = 720p² – 180πp² = 180p²(4 – π). Proportion of empty space = empty space / box volume = 180p²(4 – π) / 720p² = (4 – π) / 4. The p² terms cancel, so the proportion is independent of the radius p. Achieved = correctly states volume of 12 tins = 180πp² OR volume of box = 720p². Merit = correct expression for empty space volume = 180p²(4 – π), OR correct proportion with a minor error. Excellence = correct proportion (4 – π) / 4 with full working, clearly showing the p² cancels and the result is independent of the radius.

questions.text:
[Diagram: Point P at the bottom. Point A is 70 km directly north (above) P. Point B is 140 km directly east (to the right) of A. Triangle PAB has a right angle at A.]

Town A is 70 km due North of town P. Town B is 140 km due East of town A. Find the distance from P to B.
questions.markingGuide: P is directly south of A (70 km), and B is directly east of A (140 km). Triangle PAB has a right angle at A. Using Pythagoras: PB² = PA² + AB² = 70² + 140² = 4900 + 19600 = 24500. PB = √24500 = 156.52 km. Accept equivalent exact forms such as 70√5. Award Achieved for correct distance with working shown.

questions.text: The bearing of P from A is 120°. Find the bearing of town A from town B.
questions.expectedAnswer: Bearing of A from B is approximately 243° (accept with rounding)
questions.markingGuide: First find angle ABP using trigonometry in triangle PAB. tan(ABP) = PA / AB = 70 / 140 = 0.5. Angle ABP = arctan(0.5) = 26.57°. Since bearing of P from A is 120°, A is to the north-west of the line. The bearing of A from B requires finding the angle measured clockwise from north at B. Bearing of A from B = 270° – 26.57° = 243.43° (or equivalent valid method depending on diagram orientation). Achieved = correct angle ABP = 26.57° with working, OR correct bearing without working. Merit = correct bearing of A from B with clear trigonometric working shown.

questions.text: Ship W travels from A to P at speed k km/h. Ship V travels from A to B. The total travel time for both ships combined is 4 hours. Distance AP = 70 km, distance AB = 140 km. Find an expression for the speed of ship V in terms of k.
questions.markingGuide: Time = Distance / Speed. Time for ship W = 70 / k hours. Time for ship V = 140 / S_V hours (where S_V is the speed of ship V). Total time: 70/k + 140/S_V = 4. Rearrange for S_V: 140/S_V = 4 – 70/k = (4k – 70) / k. Therefore S_V = 140k / (4k – 70). Achieved = correct expression for time of ship W (= 70/k) OR time of ship V (= 140/S_V). Merit = correctly forming the equation 70/k + 140/S_V = 4, OR correct S_V expression with a minor algebraic error. Excellence = correct expression S_V = 140k / (4k – 70) with full algebraic working shown.

questions.text:
[Diagram: A regular octagon with all sides = 120 cm. Vertex A is at the bottom-right. Z is the midpoint of the side adjacent to A. Line ZA is drawn. Angle ZAB = v is marked at vertex A, where B is the next vertex along.]

A regular octagon has side length 120 cm. Show that the angle v (angle ZAB) equals 67.5°.
questions.markingGuide: Interior angle of a regular octagon = (n – 2) × 180° / n = (8 – 2) × 180° / 8 = 6 × 180° / 8 = 1080° / 8 = 135°. The angle ZAB is half of the interior angle (by symmetry, Z is the midpoint of one side and the line from Z to A bisects the interior angle at A). Therefore v = 135° / 2 = 67.5°. Award Achieved for clear and justified working that shows how 67.5° is obtained from the interior angle of the octagon.

questions.text:
[Diagram: Right-angled triangle ZAX inside the octagon. AZ = 120 cm (hypotenuse, a side of the octagon). Angle ZAX = 67.5°. X is the foot of the perpendicular from Z to the line AB. XZ is vertical, AX is horizontal.]

In triangle ZAX, AZ = 120 cm and angle ZAX = 67.5°. Find the lengths XZ and AX.
questions.markingGuide: Using right-angled triangle ZAX with hypotenuse AZ = 120 cm (one side of the octagon) and angle ZAX = 67.5°. For XZ (opposite side): sin 67.5° = XZ / 120, so XZ = 120 × sin 67.5° = 120 × 0.9239 = 110.87 cm. For AX (adjacent side): cos 67.5° = AX / 120, so AX = 120 × cos 67.5° = 120 × 0.3827 = 45.92 cm. Achieved = one correct length (either XZ or AX) with working. Merit = both lengths correct with clear trigonometric working shown.
